title: West Virginia's 2nd Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 race for West Virginia's 2nd Congressional District pits first-term incumbent Rep. Riley Moore (R) against Democratic nominee Ace Parsi, an Iranian immigrant and community organizer. Two independent candidates, Patrick Carney and Christopher Whitcomb, are also on the general election ballot. The district covers the Eastern Panhandle and north-central West Virginia including Morgantown, and has voted reliably Republican in recent cycles; the Cook Political Report rates the race as Solidly Republican. The Democratic primary on May 12, 2026, was closely contested, with Parsi defeating Fairmont teacher Stephanie Spears Tomana and Navy veteran Steven Wendelin by a narrow margin.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for this race as of mid-2026. The Cook Political Report rates the general election as Solidly Republican.

candidates.name: Riley Moore
candidates.summary: Riley Moore is the incumbent U.S. Representative for West Virginia's 2nd Congressional District, first elected in 2024. He previously served as West Virginia State Treasurer (2021–2025) and as a member of the West Virginia House of Delegates (2017–2019). A Republican, Moore sits on the House Appropriations Committee and is a member of the Republican Study Committee.

candidates.name: Ace Parsi
candidates.summary: Ace Parsi is the Democratic nominee for U.S. House in West Virginia's 2nd Congressional District. He immigrated from Iran with his family at age 8 and grew up in poverty. Parsi served as coalition engagement director for iCivics, a civics education nonprofit, and is a community organizer in Morgantown. He won a competitive three-way Democratic primary on May 12, 2026.

forecast.rationale: No public polls exist for this race (based_on_poll_count=0), which lowers confidence to medium. However, the available race data strongly favors Republicans: Riley Moore is the first-term incumbent in a district described as reliably Republican in recent cycles, and Cook Political Report rates the race as Solidly Republican. The Democratic nominee, Ace Parsi, won a competitive three-way primary on May 12, 2026, but no information suggests unusual Republican vulnerability in the general election. Two independent candidates (Patrick Carney, Christopher Whitcomb) are on the ballot but lack visible resources or competitive signals. Given the strong structural Republican advantage and absence of contrary indicators, a safe Republican hold is the most probable outcome.
